hook: Caesar's right-hand man, Cleopatra's lover, and Octavian's great rival.

pages.x: Marcus Antonius was born in 83 BC into a noble Roman family. As a young man he ran up huge debts and partied hard, then studied public speaking in Greece. He made his name as a bold cavalry officer, and became Caesar's right-hand man in Gaul and in the civil war.

After Caesar's murder in 44 BC, Antony gave the funeral speech in the Forum. He read out Caesar's will, which left money to every citizen, and showed the crowd his bloodstained robe. The crowd rioted and burned the body in the Forum, and the killers fled Rome. Shakespeare turned it into a famous speech.

Antony joined Caesar's heir Octavian and a third man, Lepidus, to rule Rome. They drew up lists of enemies to be killed, among them the great orator Cicero. In 42 BC at Philippi, in Greece, Antony beat Brutus and Cassius, who both took their own lives.

Antony summoned Cleopatra to Tarsus to explain herself. She sailed up the river on a barge with a golden stern, purple sails and silver oars, dressed as the goddess Venus, while flutes played. Antony fell for her, and spent the winter with her in Alexandria.

Antony ruled the East with Cleopatra and gave Roman lands to their children, which Octavian used to turn Rome against him. In 31 BC their fleet was beaten at Actium, off western Greece. When Cleopatra's ships broke away, Antony followed her.

A year later, with Octavian's army at Alexandria and his own troops deserting, Antony heard a false report that Cleopatra was dead, and fell on his sword. Dying, he was carried to her, and died in her arms.

Antony was a brave soldier and a gifted speaker whose rivalry with Octavian decided the future of Rome. His love for Cleopatra became one of the great love stories, retold by Plutarch, Shakespeare and Hollywood.
pts: Turned Rome against Caesar's killers with a funeral speech
Beat Brutus and Cassius at Philippi
His love for Cleopatra became legend
